t.5.9.1: Casting off that thought, the great monkey then became steady, and he turned to another reflection concerning Sītā.
t.5.9.2: Separated from Rāma, that beautiful lady would not deserve to sleep, nor to eat, nor even to adorn herself, nor to partake of drink.
t.5.9.4: Some women were wearied by amorous play, and others likewise by singing; still others were exhausted by dancing, and others too were overcome by drinking.
t.5.9.3: Nor would she go to another man, not even the lord of the gods, for there is none equal to Rāma even among the thirty gods. Concluding, 'This is another woman,' he wandered on through the drinking-hall.
t.5.9.5: Some women lay upon murajas and mṛdaṅgas and upon small seats, and other women likewise lay upon the finest coverlets.
t.5.9.6: It was graced by a thousand women adorned with ornaments, given to charming conversation and speaking in fitting songs and meaningful words.
t.5.9.8: In their midst the mighty-armed lord of the Rākṣasas shone forth, like a bull amid the finest cows in a great cow-pen.
t.5.9.7: The chief of the monkey troops beheld it, lying fast asleep after the delights of love-making, together with a throng attentive to place and time and given to speaking fitting words.
t.5.9.9: That lord of the Rākṣasas, himself surrounded by those women, shone forth like a great elephant in the forest encircled by she-elephants.
t.5.9.10: And in the house of that great-souled lord of the rākṣasas, the tiger among monkeys saw the drinking hall, furnished with every object of desire.
t.5.9.11: There in the drinking-hall he saw meats of deer, buffaloes and boars, laid out portion by portion.
t.5.9.12: And in wide vessels of gold the tiger among monkeys saw half-eaten peacocks and likewise cocks.
t.5.9.13: Hanumān looked upon boars and vārdhrāṇasa birds, porcupines, deer and peacocks, all prepared with curds and sauvarcala salt.
t.5.9.14: He saw various cooked kṛkara birds, half-eaten cakora partridges, buffaloes, ekaśalya fish and goats fully dressed and cooked; and there were foods to be licked of every kind, drinks, and many kinds of dishes to be eaten.
t.5.9.15: Likewise it was strewn with sour and salty relishes, with various rāgaṣāḍava sweetmeats, and with costly necklaces, anklets and armlets that had been cast aside.
t.5.9.16: With drinking vessels scattered about and with fruits of many kinds as well, the ground, strewn with offerings of flowers, displayed a still greater splendour.
t.5.9.17: With couches and seats well joined together and placed here and there, the drinking hall appeared as if ablaze even without fire.
t.5.9.18: It was furnished with meats of many kinds and great variety, dressed with the finest preparations and skillfully combined, set out separately across the drinking ground.
t.5.9.20: The ground shone, strewn with garlands placed in many spots, and covered with golden water-jars, crystal vessels, and other pitchers made of jāmbūnada gold.
t.5.9.19: There were divine wines of many kinds, clear liquors and prepared spirits as well: sugar-spirits, honey-wines, flower-spirits and fruit-spirits, each one separately refined with various fragrant powders.
t.5.9.21: Then the monkey saw there an abundance of the finest drink in jars made of silver and of Jāmbūnada gold.
t.5.9.22: The great monkey saw vessels of gold, vessels made of gems, and vessels of silver, all filled with sīdhu liquor.
t.5.9.23: He saw drinks that were in some places half left, in some places drunk up entirely, and in some places not drunk at all.
t.5.9.24: He wandered about, seeing here various kinds of food, there drinks set out in separate portions, and elsewhere the leftovers of the meal.
t.5.9.25: In some places it was strewn with shattered water-pots, in others with overturned jars, and in places he saw garlands mingled together with water and fruits.
t.5.9.27: And one young woman, snatching away another's garment and wrapping herself in it, drew close to her and lay asleep, overcome by the power of sleep.
t.5.9.26: Here, again, he saw the women's couches lying empty in many places, while some lovely women slept locked in each other's embrace.
t.5.9.28: Stirred by the breath of their exhalations, the garments and garlands on their bodies flutter only slightly, as though touched by a soft and lovely breeze.
t.5.9.30: There the wind, bearing in many ways a varied fragrance of bathing unguents, of sandal pastes and of incense, blew intensified, and a sweet fragrance then pervaded the aerial chariot Puṣpaka.
t.5.9.29: There was the fragrance of cool sandalwood, of sīdhu liquor and of honey-sweet juice, of garlands of many kinds and of flowers of many kinds.
t.5.9.31: There in the abode of the Rākṣasa, other lovely women were dusky or fair, some were dark, and some young women had limbs the colour of gold.
t.5.9.32: Because they were under the sway of sleep, and overcome by passion, their appearance was truly just like that of lotus plants that have closed in sleep.
t.5.9.33: Thus the monkey of exceedingly great splendour saw the whole of Rāvaṇa's inner apartments without leaving anything out, and yet he did not see Jānakī.
t.5.9.34: Then, as he gazed upon those women, the great monkey fell into deep anxiety, troubled by the fear that he had transgressed dharma.
t.5.9.35: This gazing upon the sleeping harem of another's wives will surely bring about a grave violation of dharma on my part.
t.5.9.36: For my gaze has never strayed toward the wives of others as objects of desire, and yet here I have looked upon this whole gathering of another's wives.
t.5.9.37: Then yet another thought arose in that high-minded one, whose mind was firmly and single-pointedly resolved, a thought that revealed to him certainty about what had to be done.
t.5.9.38: True, all of Rāvaṇa's women, resting unguarded and at ease, have been seen by me; yet not the slightest disturbance arises in my mind.
t.5.9.39: For it is the mind that acts as the cause of all the senses in good and evil states alike, and that mind of mine is firmly composed.
t.5.9.40: For nowhere else could Vaidehī be searched for by me; indeed, in any search, women are always to be found among women.
t.5.9.41: Whatever the species to which a creature belongs, it is among that very kind that it is searched for; a lost woman cannot be sought among female deer.
t.5.9.42: This entire inner apartment of Rāvaṇa has thus been searched by me with a pure mind, and yet Jānakī is not seen.
t.5.9.43: Though the valiant Hanumān gazed upon the daughters of the devas and gandharvas and the daughters of the nāgas, he did not see Jānakī.
t.5.9.44: Not seeing her there, though seeing other excellent women, the heroic monkey then withdrew and began to reflect deeply.
